**This is individual work.** Everyone produces their own page. The final project is where you work
in a team; the studio is where the thinking gets into your own hands.
:::

The session runs to a fixed clock: **Answer** 20 minutes, **Generate** 20, **Reconcile** 25, **peer
check** 10. The move from Answer to Generate is called at minute 20 whether or not you finished — an
unfinished answer is a legitimate finding, and you will report it as one.

::: {.part}
### Part 1 · Before you arrive

Accounts and installs. Do these before Thursday, not during it. Nothing here is graded, and nothing
here is part of SA1 — but Week 3 and Week 4 assume it is already done.

1. Claim your AI access: register the free student year at [gemini.google/students](https://gemini.google/students/) if you are eligible. If you are not, the free tier is sufficient for every studio in this course — say so on your page so it is on record.
2. Create a Taiga account at [tree.taiga.io](https://tree.taiga.io) with your NDSU email, and a private project named `IMSE456-yourlastname`. You will use it from Week 3.
3. Install [ProjectLibre](https://www.projectlibre.com/) and open it once to confirm it launches. If it fails on your machine it fails *today*, not in Week 4 — [GanttProject](https://www.ganttproject.biz/) is the sanctioned fallback and costs you nothing.
4. Create the cloud folder you will use all semester — Google Drive or OneDrive, named `IMSE456`. **Everything in this course is saved there, never to a local disk.**
5. Open the access form linked on Blackboard: which machine you will work on, and which AI tooling you can reach. Two minutes, no effect on your grade — it decides which version of every later lab sheet you get.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 2 · What you leave with

**SA1 — one page.** Not two. The five review questions from the week page answered in your own
words, a record of where the model helped and where it was wrong, and the acknowledgement block.

The page limit is the exercise. Anyone can generate four pages in nine seconds.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 3 · Answer first, unaided — 20 minutes

**You go first. The model goes second.** That order is the whole point, and reversing it destroys
the only data this studio produces.

Open the [five review questions](../weeks/week-01.qmd#review-questions) on the week page. Close
every other tab.

1. Answer **all five** from the reading and the Tuesday session. Rough notes are fine — full
   sentences are not required yet.
2. Where you are unsure, write **"unsure"** and move on. Do not guess to fill the space.
3. Where you cannot answer at all, write **"no answer"**.

Those two marks are the most valuable thing on the page at minute 20. Keep this draft — you are
going to compare against it, and you cannot reconstruct it afterwards.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 4 · Now bring the model in — 20 minutes

1. Give the model the same five questions. Ask for its answers.
2. For **every** question — including the ones you were confident about — ask it one follow-up that
   pushes on something specific: *"which of the five characteristics does that example actually
   fail?"*, *"give me a counter-example"*, *"what would change your answer?"*
3. Pick **one exercise** from the week page and work it with the model's help.
4. Keep the transcript, or the link to it. You need it for the acknowledgement.

Ask it for its sources on any factual claim — a number, a date, a study. Then check one of them
against the chapter. Note what you find, whichever way it goes.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 5 · Reconcile, and write the page — 25 minutes

This is the graded part. Everything before it was raw material.

For each of the five questions, decide what you now believe and **write that** — your answer, not
the model's, and not a merge of the two performed without deciding.

Then account for the difference. On the page, name:

- **At least one place the model was wrong**, incomplete, or confidently vague. Say what was wrong
  with it. "It was generic" is not specific enough; "it defined a program as any set of projects and
  dropped the common-goal requirement, which is what separates a program from a portfolio" is.
- **At least one place it changed your mind**, and what specifically moved you.
- **Every question you marked "unsure" at minute 20** — say whether you are still unsure, and if
  not, what resolved it.

If the model was right about everything, you did not push hard enough in Part 4, and you should say
so on the page rather than pretend otherwise. That is a legitimate finding and it is graded as one.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 6 · Done looks like — the checklist your neighbour runs on you at minute 65

- [ ] one page, and genuinely one page
- [ ] all five review questions answered in your own words
- [ ] one exercise worked
- [ ] at least one specific model error named, with what was wrong with it
- [ ] at least one place the model changed your mind
- [ ] every minute-20 "unsure" accounted for
- [ ] the AI acknowledgement block, with tool and transcript link
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 7 · Where it is saved

`IMSE456/studio-01/` in your cloud folder. Name the file `SA1_yourlastname.pdf`.

**Nothing in this course is saved to a local disk.** Lab machines wipe on reboot and laptops get
left at home. Your page is read in the session itself — there is no separate submission afterwards.
:::

::: {.browser-path}
**Working on a lab machine, or without your own device?**

Everything in this studio runs in a browser. Write the page in Google Docs or Word Online and export
to PDF at the end. No install is needed for SA1 — the installs in Part 1 are for later weeks.
:::

## Study loop for this week

Run this before you read the notes, and again after. It is not graded; it is the fastest way to find
out what you have wrong.

```text
Be my tutor on the difference between a project and an operation. Ask me
one question at a time. Don't lecture. Start by making me state the test,
then hand me cases that break it — a film studio, a release train, a
refinery shutdown — until I stop treating it as a fact about the world.
```

See [AI Studio](../ai.qmd) for the Editor and Roommate prompts and the full loop.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**Label it, verify it, own it.** Append the AI acknowledgement block from the [syllabus](../syllabus.qmd#how-to-disclose): the tool, the prompt or transcript link, what you changed after reviewing its output, and what it got wrong. Every quantitative result arrives with the check that proves it — **the check is graded, not the output**. "The model said so" is not a defence in this course or in a project review.
:::
